title: OpenAI compatibility: function aliasing and stream message-stitching
author: Lena Ortiz
description: Add an OpenAI-compatibility shim that introduces function aliasing and deterministic message-stitching for fragmented streaming envelopes. Motivation: customers are seeing mismatches between tool selection and schema mapping when upstream model providers emit fragmented function call messages across multiple stream events or when function names change in model-provided metadata. This PR implements a small, opt-in compatibility layer that 1) resolves function aliases (alias table + canonical resolver) so servers and downstream tool routers see stable identifiers even when the model emits legacy or variant names, 2) stitches fragmented function call payloads across stream frames into a single canonical invocation envelope before tool selection and schema validation, and 3) adds deterministic tiebreaker ordering for tool_choice when multiple candidate functions match (based on alias priority, explicit schema match score, and stable timestamp ordering). The shim preserves original raw fragments for auditing and includes a compact reassembly log in tracing. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged unless the new config flag openai_compat.alias_stitch is enabled per-route or per-customer. This PR updates the OpenAI adapter layer, the streaming demuxer, the tool-routing matcher, and unit/integration tests. Includes a migration toggle and docs note explaining tradeoffs and the conditions under which the shim should be enabled. Rollout: staged rollout behind the feature flag, Canary in us-west-2 on dedicated, then gradual expansion with observability flags to detect any drift in tool invocation rates across tenants.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Overall approach LGTM; question about CPU impact of reassembly on high-qps routes — can we early-drop if fragment metadata indicates a mismatched invocation?

Lena Ortiz: Reply: we early-validate the function name/schema on the first fragment and short-circuit reassembly for clearly invalid shards; added a benchmark + guard in reassembly.go (see commit b3e1974)
Ellen Zhang: nits on test naming and a request to add a unit test for alias collisions where two functions differ only by punctuation — added f2c0041 to cover this
Priya Menon: Approving after a small tweak to the feature flag name to be per-route rather than global — changed flag in a4c11f8
release_notes: Introduce opt-in OpenAI compatibility shim: function alias resolution + stream fragment reassembly. Controlled by config openai_compat.alias_stitch; recommended for customers experiencing fragmented function call envelopes or model-side naming variants.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for alias resolution, fragment reassembly, and deterministic tool_choice tie-breaking; added integration test that simulates fragmented stream delivery with reordered frames; ran canary benchmark showing median P95 latency increase <= 1.2% when reassembly is enabled (reassembly guarded by early-validation to avoid work on invalid frames).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag merged gated behind openai_compat.alias_stitch. 2) Enable in canary (us-west-2 dedicated) for 48 hours with alerting on tool invocation rate delta and error rate. 3) If stable, enable for 10% of production traffic for 24 hours. 4) Gradually widen with daily checks. Provide rollback path by toggling flag or disabling at route-level.
